title: SIEM export failure-injection test matrix and customer validation runbook
body:
Purpose:
This working runbook captures a failure-injection and negative-testing matrix for SIEM export connectors (Splunk HC/HEC, Datadog Events, Azure Sentinel/Log Analytics). The goal is twofold: 1) provide a repeatable set of tests we run before customer onboarding and 2) define observable acceptance criteria for evidence automation, RBAC v2 mappings, and PII/field-redaction safeguards.

Audience:
Eng owners of connector integrations, SRE/observability, security & compliance reviewers, and solutions engineers validating customer onboarding.

Scope:
- Connectors: Splunk HEC (TLS+Token), Datadog Events/Logs API, Azure Sentinel ingestion via Event Hubs/HTTP Data Collector API.
- Functional areas: network/auth, TLS/cert rotation, schema/field validation, RBAC-mapping propagation, evidence automation triggers, delivery guarantees (exactly-once/at-least-once), throttling/backpressure, and metadata/time-drift handling.
- Exclusions: upstream cloud provider outages outside our control; those are handled by cloud status pages and separate incident runbooks.

How to use this doc (notes to self):
- Run the matrix in a staging environment that mirrors customer routing policies (region, SNI, vip, proxy).
- Where possible use customer-provided sample payloads saved in /test-fixtures/siem-customers/* and annotate differences.
- Capture traces & token-level cost during test to validate telemetry hooks.

Test categories and example failure scenarios (matrix):
1) Connectivity and Transport
  - Scenario: TCP/UDP transient packet loss (10-30% loss window for 30s).
    Steps: use tc/netem or proxy failure injection between runtime and egress.
    Expected: buffer/backpressure triggers batching fallback; telemetry shows request retries; no silent data loss beyond configured retention window.
    Observability signals: increased request latency, 429s or 500s at connector, retry counters increment, backlog queue depth metric rises.

  - Scenario: Baseline MTU mismatch / fragmentation causing occasional truncated payloads.
    Steps: force lower MTU on the connector host; send large batched payloads.
    Expected: connector should detect truncated responses and mark events for re-send or move to DLQ. Error count metric and DLQ entries should be observable.

2) Auth & RBAC propagation
  - Scenario: Token rotation mid-flight (Splunk HEC/Datadog API key rotated).
    Steps: rotate token in secret store, invalidate current token via API, continue sending.
    Expected: brief spike in auth failures; connector auto-reloads secrets and resumes; no event duplication.
    Acceptance: failure window < 2 minutes for hosted flows, <5 minutes for dedicated/private with eventual success for buffered items.

  - Scenario: RBAC v2 mapping regression where 'auditor' role lost write-to-log permission causing missing audit entries.
    Steps: simulate role change in test tenant (RBAC v2 policy modify), send audit events.
    Expected: connector should log permission errors, create evidence-automation alerts, and mark impacted events; solutions team notified automatically via PagerDuty/Slack channel.

3) Schema and Field Validation
  - Scenario: Missing required fields (timestamp, event_id) in 5% of messages.
    Steps: mutate test payload generator to drop fields randomly; ingest.
    Expected: connector validates, rejects or tags malformed records, and routes to DLQ with canonical error reason. Evidence automation should flag affected records and not silently drop them.

  - Scenario: PII leakage (email/SSN present in freeform message field) despite redaction pipeline enabled.
    Steps: send payloads containing PII patterns; simulate redaction service slowed/failed.
    Expected: connector must escalate (create evidence item and mark policy violation). For hosted customers, redact at proxy level where feasible and pause export until mitigation.

4) Delivery semantics and duplicates
  - Scenario: Duplicate events delivered due to upstream retry + connector crash and restart.
    Steps: set very short ack window, cause connector process crash, then restart.
    Expected: idempotency keys used to deduplicate where supported (Splunk event_id, Datadog event_stream ids). Tests must verify dedupe success rate > 99.9% for non-malformed payloads.

5) Throttling and backpressure
  - Scenario: Target API returns 429 for sustained period (1 minute to 10 minutes).
    Steps: configure mock backend to return 429 with Retry-After header; ramp sender throughput.
    Expected: connector respects Retry-After, reduces send rate, tracks throttled bytes, and exposes per-tenant backpressure metrics. For Dedicated customers, overflow should use burst capacity policy if enabled.

6) Time drift and ordering
  - Scenario: Source clocks skewed by > 2 hours (simulate client with wrong system time).
    Steps: send events with manually set timestamps far in past/future.
    Expected: connector normalizes timestamps based on ingestion time policy or tags events with original timestamp and ingestion_time. Evidence-automation should be able to correlate by ingestion_time when ordering matters.

7) Evidence automation-specific scenarios
  - Scenario: Trigger rule misfires (rule uses field 'user.email' instead of 'actor.email').
    Steps: deploy mis-configured rule in staging, send matching events.
    Expected: automation does not suppress other alerts; misfire count is observable; a validation job detects field mismatches during onboarding.

  - Scenario: Evidence batching window exceeds SLA (batch stored > 10 minutes before processing).
    Steps: slow downstream processing nodes; observe batch latency.
    Expected: automation escalates to ops channel and falls back to single-item flush until processing resumes.

Failure injection tooling and quick commands (notes):
- Network emulation: tc qdisc netem (Linux) or toxiproxy for application layer faults. Example:
  - tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 20% delay 500ms
  - toxiproxy: create proxy and add latency/limit rules in test harness.
- Mock backends: use local httpbin or wiremock; for Azure use Azure Storage emulator or Mock Event Hub.
- Secret rotation: use HashiCorp Vault dev instance and simulate token revoke endpoints.
- DLQ inspection: use jq + bat to sample entries and verify error meta.

Sample checklists for a single customer onboarding test run:
- Pre-checks:
  - Customer sample payloads uploaded (path noted)
  - Test credentials and test tenant provisioned
  - Observability dashboards created and baseline captured (latency, retry, DLQ rate)
- Run failure-injection scenarios defined above in order of increasing impact
- Post-run:
  - Collect logs, traces, and DLQ samples
  - Create a validation report with pass/fail per scenario and attach to Jira ticket
  - If failures are beyond acceptable thresholds, pause onboarding and escalate to connector owner

Acceptance criteria (suggested):
- Auth failure window: automatic recovery within 5 minutes for hosted, 15 minutes for private unless customer SLA states otherwise.
- No silent data loss: any rejected/unprocessed records must be visible in DLQ with error reason and trace id.
- Evidence automation accuracy: false positive rate < 0.5% during test corpus; false negative rate TBD (discuss with product).
- RBAC mapping verification: all mapped audit events must be visible to auditor role in downstream SIEM within expected propagation window (< 60s for hosted paths).

Operational playbacks and rollback guidance:
- If connector crash causes large DLQ backlog, throttle ingestion from source (smart-routing policy) and increase consumer parallelism to clear backlog.
- Backout path: restore previous connector container image + configuration from last known-good tag; rotate keys if suspected compromise.

Reporting artifact templates (what to attach to Jira when filing regression):
- Short summary (one line)
- Steps to reproduce minimum set (copyable commands)
- Attached logs: connector stdout + connector traces + DLQ sample (max 10 entries)
- Metrics snapshot: baseline vs during-failure (latency, error rate, retries)
- Suggested mitigation and owner

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- What is the canonical idempotency key for Azure Sentinel ingestion? Need to standardize across all connectors. (Action: @Liam to raise PR GH:infra/connector-specs).
- Formalize evidence-automation acceptance thresholds with Product (false negative target).
- Should we auto-pause exports on PII-detection by default for hosted customers? Confirm legal/ops opinion.

References and links:
- GH:redwood-infra/siem-connectors (implementation repo)
- JIRA:SEC-912 (evidence automation alerting gaps)
- Confluence: SIEM export spec (canonical field list and redaction guidance)
- Slack: #sec-siem (thread: 2026-02-18 export-throttling-postmortem)

Appendix — Example malformed event (copy-paste test payload):
{
  "event_id": null,
  "timestamp": "2026-03-01T15:22:00Z",
  "actor": { "email": "bad@example.com", "id": 123 },
  "message": "Customer note containing SSN 123-45-6789"
}

Notes to onboarding engineers (quick):
- Always run schema validation locally before enabling production export.
- Keep a tight feedback loop with solutions engineering while running these negative tests — customer expectations vary.
- Capture a short Loom for any non-trivial failures to accelerate triage.

End of draft.
